hypotheses.reasoning: At 01:15:00 search-api hot-reloaded config revision 747 from config-service, changing CATALOG_SVC_URL to http://catalog-svc.internal:8081. This was a runtime config push, not a versioned release. The last successful catalog call was at 01:15:18, which was probably still in flight on the old connection. From 01:16:03 on, every catalog-svc call from search-api gets connection refused on 10.23.138.197:8081. catalog-svc stays healthy the whole time: it keeps logging GC pauses at normal heap levels and has no errors, but it gets no requests after 01:15:18. That points to the new port/endpoint being wrong, not catalog-svc going down. search-api then returns 503s, and web-bff's GET /search fails (the alert). Unrelated: the auth-svc S3 500/503 errors only break /login through account-svc. Also unrelated: the long-running status-poller legacy-inventory timeouts and one index-worker DLQ message at 01:07.
Someone could read the config revision push as a change rollout. But no version or release appears in the logs; it is a config-service reload.
S3 in us-east-1 is returning 500/503 errors to auth-svc. This explains the separate /login failures but not /search.

verdict.recommendedAction: Roll back config-service revision 747 for search-api, i.e. set CATALOG_SVC_URL back to the correct catalog-svc port, and confirm search-api can connect to catalog-svc again. Add validation or a canary for config-service pushes. Handle the S3 failures in auth-svc (/login) as a separate incident.
